author: Inside Edition
description: Passenger Lacinda Thackery was looking out the terminal window at John Wayne Airport in southern California and was startled to see a limping worker making his way across the tarmac. She says she was struck by the fact that he was clearly struggling to walk but was still working hard. Thackeray posted a video online and it did not take long for social media to do its magic. The worker's name is James Blair. He is a 64-year-old Navy vet who works at the airport refueling planes. He spoke with Inside Edition. A GoFundMe page started by Thackery has so far raised $83,000 and counting.
title: GoFundMe Raises Funds To Help Airplane Mechanic Struggling To Do His Job

author: Inside Edition
description: A mom convicted of hosting alcohol-fueled sex parties for teens is set to be sentenced on Thursday. A jury found Shannon O'Connor guilty on 48 counts including child endangerment and sexual battery. Mom Sherri Mullin says her daughter attended two of the parties at O'Connor's mansion. She spoke to Inside Edition exclusively before the sentencing. Mullin read her daughter's victim impact statement to Inside Edition.
title: Mom Convicted Of Hosting Alcohol-Fueled Sex Parties For Teens Set To Be Sentenced

author: Inside Edition
description: Nurse Melanie Smith was in court on Long Island Thursday and came face to face with the man she says has been relentlessly stalking her. Michael Pacek, a 47-year-old truck driver, is charged with stalking, aggravated harassment, and criminal contempt. Police said they could do little to protect Smith, but after she told her story to Inside Edition last week, Pacek was put in handcuffs. Pacek did not enter a plea and was ordered held without bail.
title: Woman Comes Face-To-Face With Man She Says Has Been Relentlessly Stalking Her

author: Inside Edition
description: It's getting hot in here, and scientists say that's not going to change anytime soon. The United Nations' climate agency says over the next five years, global temperatures are very likely to rise nearly three degrees Fahrenheit, or one and a half degrees celsius, higher than they did in pre-industrial times. Scientists say it's well past time to take action. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: UN Climate Scientists Say Hottest Year Record Could Be Broken In Next 5 Years

author: Inside Edition
description: A woman makes a compelling case for why she shouldn't get a traffic ticket. CBS News obtained this bodycam video of a traffic stop in Palm Beach County, Florida. The deputy explains to the driver that he saw her driving with a phone in her right hand. When the driver, Kathleen Thomas, presents her right arm, missing a hand, she seems to have good reason to question what the deputy actually saw. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Woman Without A Right Hand Fights Citation For Driving With Phone In Right Hand

author: Inside Edition
description: Need help finding and cooking the best possible cut for your summer cookout? INSIDE EDITION spoke with Chopped Champion Lauren Covas to learn the secrets to picking the best steak at your grocery store, finding beautifully marbled steaks and the right thickness for you. Then, Chef Dan Souza of America’s Test Kitchen told us how you can make your steak taste delicious by providing us with his expert tips and tricks to seasoning and cooking.
title: The Secrets Of Steak: How To Pick And Cook The Best Beef This Summer

author: Inside Edition
description: High school students in Tennessee graduated in the pouring rain. Some were unhappy that the once in a lifetime event went ahead despite the weather. Mother Britney Garner tells Inside Edition she kicked her shoes off and walked onto the field to stand over her daughter with her umbrella. "I just couldn't believe this was happening," Garner says. But others, like graduate Ben Harris, say the rain made it a fun event. "If it can bring some hope to people that you can truly weather the storm, both literally and metaphorically, then it's worth it," Harris' mother Andrea Hutchinson says.
title: High School Students Graduate In The Pouring Rain

author: Inside Edition
description: Police in Texas had their work cut out for them. This suspect had a big advantage during a chase. That's because kangaroos can sprint up to 45 miles per hour and jump up to six feet in the air. The Waco Police say the escape artist got out of its enclosure and hopped around the neighborhood. All units responded to this scene after the marsupial was spotted at a car dealership. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Cops Chase Runaway Kangaroo Through Neighborhood Until It's Caught
